description.value: The Tunnel of Flags is a historic one-lane road tunnel in Greenwood, BC, dating to 1913, that was rediscovered above ground after a new road was built in 1993. To combat graffiti, then-mayor Arno Hennig launched a community project that resulted in 210 hand-painted country flags covering the exterior walls by 2000. It is a quirky and photogenic roadside stop in Canada's smallest city, easily accessible to passing cyclists on the Crowsnest Highway corridor.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is a 2017 feature article about the Tunnel of Flags' history — it is not a visitor services page and contains no mention of bike parking, washrooms, water, or any cyclist amenities. The attraction is described as an outdoor roadside structure (a historic tunnel painted with 210 country flags by community volunteers) with no staff or facilities implied. OSM tags provide only the name and website URL; no address, phone, or amenity tags are present.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The Tunnel of Flags is a legitimate and notable cycling waypoint on the Crowsnest corridor, but it is an unstaffed outdoor roadside structure with no confirmed amenities; it cannot be verified as meeting any WWC required criteria. A human reviewer should assess whether the directory includes amenity-free points of interest and whether bike parking or washrooms exist nearby in downtown Greenwood.
enrichment_extras.notes: This is an unattended, free, outdoor community art installation. The City of Greenwood or Greenwood Museum may be better OSM contacts for confirming nearby amenities and current condition.
